title: Normalized direct-image/reduction square on adjunction Hom groups
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:Z\to X$ be a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and the completed coefficient sheaves $R_W=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ for $W=Z,X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $F=Rf_{*,R}$ for ordinary completed-ring direct image, $F_n=Rf_{*,A_n}$ for finite direct image, $K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_W}(A_n)_W$, and $\operatorname{Res}_{W,n}$ for restriction along $R_W\to(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, def-weil-integral-derived-reduction, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $c_{W,K,n}:K\to\operatorname{Res}_{W,n}K_n$ be the actual scalar-adjunction unit [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction].

Let $\alpha_{n,M}:F\operatorname{Res}_{Z,n}M\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{X,n}F_nM$ be the normalized derived-composition comparison, coherent for all quotient restrictions, of [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison]. Let $P$ be derived $t$-complete [def-weil-derived-complete], and let $\beta_{n,P}:(FP)_n\xrightarrow{\sim}F_nP_n$ be the canonical projection-formula comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits], using this coefficient identification. For $m\in\mathbf Z$, transport shifts through these exact functors.

For every $M\in D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ and $u:P_n[m]\to M$ one has the equality in the completed-ring derived category on $X$
$$
 \alpha_{n,M}\circ F(\operatorname{Res}_{Z,n}(u)\circ c_{Z,P[m],n})
 =\operatorname{Res}_{X,n}(F_n(u)\circ\beta_{n,P[m]})\circ c_{X,FP[m],n}.
$$
Thus under the two extension/restriction adjunction bijections, the map $h\mapsto\alpha_{n,M}F(h)$ is exactly $u\mapsto F_n(u)\circ\beta_{n,P[m]}$. For every derived-complete $Q$, these identifications with $M=Q_n$ commute with the transitions $\operatorname{Res}_{Z,n+1}Q_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{Z,n}Q_n$ and their image transitions on $X$. No full faithfulness of restriction of scalars is asserted.

proof.text: Put $T=P[m]$ and suppress the canonical exact-functor shift identifications. The finite quotient sheaves are finite rings by the coefficient datum in the statement, so [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] identifies their inverse images, the completed rings, and their projection maps. Thus its hypotheses give the ring-sheaf-change square. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], its direct-image comparison is $d=\alpha_n^{-1}$ and respects the geometric derived adjunctions. Write $\pi_{n,T}:\operatorname{Res}_{X,n}(FT)_n\to F\operatorname{Res}_{Z,n}T_n$ for the completed-ring projection mate. Then $\pi_{n,T}=\alpha_{n,T_n}^{-1}\operatorname{Res}_{X,n}(\beta_{n,T})$: both maps have geometric adjoint equal to the geometric counit at $T$ tensored with the finite coefficient identity, using the coefficient-change counit compatibility just cited. The scalar tensor/pullback identification is the one in that ring-sheaf square. The last paragraph of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] specifies this same mate as evaluation of its derived strict-tower morphism. This checks the normalization, rather than choosing an isomorphism merely because the two objects agree.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-augmented-diagram-projection-mate] with source $Z$, target $X$, rings $R_Z,R_X$, and algebra tower $((A_n)_X)_n$; the preceding coefficient identities identify its pulled-back tower with $((A_n)_Z)_n$. Evaluate $h_Ti_{X,FT}=F^{\rm Tow}(i_{Z,T})\chi_T$ at $n$. Evaluations of $\chi_T$ are identities by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-tower-pushforward-normalization]. The augmentations evaluate to the actual scalar units $c$ of [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction]. Hence $\pi_{n,T}c_{X,FT,n}=F(c_{Z,T,n})$. Step 1 and composition with $\alpha_{n,T_n}$ give $\operatorname{Res}_{X,n}(\beta_{n,T})c_{X,FT,n}=\alpha_{n,T_n}F(c_{Z,T,n})$.

proof.text: For $u:T_n\to M$, naturality of the coefficient comparison [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] gives $\alpha_{n,M}F(\operatorname{Res}_{Z,n}u)=\operatorname{Res}_{X,n}(F_nu)\alpha_{n,T_n}$. Compose with $F(c_{Z,T,n})$ and use Step 2. Functoriality yields exactly $\alpha_{n,M}F(\operatorname{Res}_{Z,n}(u)c_{Z,T,n})=\operatorname{Res}_{X,n}(F_n(u)\beta_{n,T})c_{X,FT,n}$. In an adjunction the transpose of $u$ is restriction of $u$ composed with its unit. The two bijections of [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction] therefore identify the two Hom maps as asserted.

proof.text: For $M=Q_n$, write $s_Z:\operatorname{Res}_{Z,n+1}Q_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{Z,n}Q_n$ for the quotient transition of [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], and $s_X$ for the corresponding finite-direct-image transition after restriction to $R_X$. Quotient coherence in [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] says $s_X\alpha_{n+1,Q_{n+1}}=\alpha_{n,Q_n}F(s_Z)$. Thus for every $h:T\to\operatorname{Res}_{Z,n+1}Q_{n+1}$, $\alpha_{n,Q_n}F(s_Zh)=s_X\alpha_{n+1,Q_{n+1}}F(h)$. This is the required commuting Hom square before scalar transposition. To specify its finite-coefficient transition, let $r_Z:D(A_n)\to D(A_{n+1})$ be restriction along $A_{n+1}\to A_n$. Let $a_{K}:K_{n+1}\to r_ZK_n$ be the quotient scalar unit followed by the normalized successive-reduction isomorphism. By [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization], $\operatorname{Res}_{Z,n+1}(a_K)c_{Z,K,n+1}=c_{Z,K,n}$. If $u:T_{n+1}\to Q_{n+1}$ transposes to $h$, its transition $v:T_n\to Q_n$ is uniquely characterized by $r_Z(v)a_T=a_Qu$, using [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] for the quotient scalar adjunction. Therefore $\operatorname{Res}_{Z,n}(v)c_{Z,T,n}=s_Zh$. The identical formula on $X$, and the displayed commuting square, prove compatibility under both adjunction bijections. No full faithfulness of restriction is used.

Step 1: the projection equation of profinite-coefficient-inverse-image (A_n is finite) is the hypothesis of ring-sheaf-change-adjunction. Its d equals alpha^{-1}, since both come from the same two factorizations. Both maps have the same adjoint, the counit tensored with the coefficient identity, and direct-image-limits says its finite maps are evaluations of the diagram mate. The adic datum fits: O_E is Noetherian and t^n-quotients are finite and perfect. Step 2: evaluate the augmented-mate equation at n. chi evaluates to the identity, the augmentation i_T evaluates to the scalar unit c, and naturality of beta_n gives the G^Tow evaluation. The result is pi c_X = F(c_Z), with no perfectness needed. Step 3 is naturality of alpha plus the transpose formula; no full faithfulness is used. Step 4: s_Z is Res(a_Q) by the representative formula of successive-quotient-normalization. The nonflat quotient adjunction gives Res(v)c_n = s_Z h, quotient coherence of alpha gives the square, and injectivity of the transpose gives F_n(v)beta_n. Edge cases (n=1, zero objects, f=id, shifts) pass. No duplicates found among the cbc reduction-unit node, complete-direct-image-reduction, target-augmentation and the sibling scalar comparison. There is no cycle, proof_deps equals the union of the uses, and I accept the ten tool_uses as generic normalization tools. No changes made.
